utterances.text: I think it's about the use of a tank which was the main gist of the question, but you have answered the question so -- and you have now added something. You may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. Because we'll resume at ten minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that all the confusion is not reflected rightly on the transcript, where, when the Judges entered the courtroom, were informed that the courtroom was not entirely ready yet. That all is now behind us. We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just to update Your Honour, I wasn't, although I was optimistic, able to find information about the location of the Pavkovic motel and I believe my friend will take that up in his re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, then we'll wait for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now I have just two quick questions to finish up, Mr. Draskovic. First of all, when you -- when your units used their machine-guns and their infantry weapons, you're not saying they only used them at elevations. They used them at ground-level targets as well. They fired at ground-level targets as well; right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: You probably did not understand me well. I did not say that we only targeted something at elevations but that the machine-guns were placed at elevations from which they had command of the area on our side.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. Then I have one last question for you. And it's because you alluded to the feeling of being under sniper fire and I just want to ask you a couple of things about that. You would agree with me, I think, from your experience that being under sniper fire would make civilians feel scared and insecure, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, both soldiers and civilians. You know what it's like if you are targeted by snipers 24 hours a day and you cannot move. You cannot be focussed enough around the clock to always be aware from which direction, what sniper is active.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It would terrorise them; right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that would be the case anywhere, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Including for those civilians who were living in Bosnian-held Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. The war caused damage and problems on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton. Mr. Stojanovic, any questions in re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Draskovic, during cross-examination, at page 43 of the temporary transcript, lines 8 and 9, you discussed the targeting of the mobile targets. What I want to ask you is this: What do you understand to be a mobile target, or, in other words, mobile artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, there were smaller cargo vehicles where mortars were mounted. For the most part they were 82-millimetre calibre and engaged the positions of the VRS. They were mounted on vehicles which could easily move and that is why we had difficulty detecting them. As I said, when they were active at night, our observers could see their location and would then inform the company and battalion commands, and then we asked that our mortars be used to neutralize theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While trying to neutralize these mobile targets, these mobile mortars, did you, at any point in time, target civilian targets with the intention not to engage a mobile target but a civilian target?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your experience as the company commander, were there ever situations in which members of the ABiH army misused, so to speak, their civilian population by using civilian facilities to target the VRS?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, certainly. They opened fire from apartment buildings, thus abusing and placing in danger their civilian population because they must have expected that we would retaliate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Through such acts and conduct of the enemy side, could you observe a system they used to engage your side by misusing the civilian facilities?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: They mostly used civilian buildings in the area of my company and in other areas from where the ABiH was active because on their side, there had been no military buildings before the war, as there are none now. Thus, they were active from civilian buildings, and we returned fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the use of 60 -- the 60-millimetre mortar that was in your company, was it fixed throughout the war or, depending on the intensity of fighting, was there any need for you to move the mortar?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: It was fixed, as I said in Ozrenska Street in the area of the 3rd Platoon of the 3rd Company. There were probably moments when it needed to be -- moved to the areas of other companies. But, as I said, for the most part, it was in the area of the 3rd Platoon of the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, another example of already giving the reasons of why the witness is supposed to answer the question in a certain way; it is the intensity of fighting which would cause it. I leave it to that. But please try to properly examine the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At page 50 of today's transcript, the temporary transcript that is, you discussed the concept of using sniping fire to terrorise on both sides. In your view, the term "terror," what does it specifically entail, if you can clarify?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: The very fact that we were defending our homes, our families, and that our positions were in front of our houses and that we had never been given an order to carry out offensive operations, and, on the other said, as I said a number of times, we had sniping around the clock, and a very uncomfortable way of living under their fire because one could not be certain at any point during the 24 hours, for example, even our guards were not safe in their posts, although they had fortifications. But there was always some window of opportunity for the sharpshooters having night-vision, hence, we were exposed to their fire round the clock and we were unable to move. That very fact that one is just waiting for your wrong step at any point in time that can end your life makes you feel very uncomfortable, and that is how this terror occurred on the side of our soldiers and civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As you could assess the war-time situation from your positions, during the war years, who was better equipped in terms of sniping rifles and who had better trained sharpshooters, the VRS or the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: The advantage was on the ABiH side throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Logically the next question follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first seek clarification of this question. What do you know about the number and the training of ABiH sharpshooters or snipers? How many were there? How many sniper rifles were used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The very fact that they could cover our positions around the clock speaks for itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... no. I'm asking you a question and I'd like to have an answer to my question. Do you know - if you don't know, that's an answer as well - how many snipers were there, on the ABiH side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not in a position to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many sniper rifles did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm also not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many sniper rifles did the Bosnian Serb army have around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I said that we had a sniping squad in our platoon comprising 12 men. I don't know if each had their own rifle or if they used the same rifles in different shifts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... were they all the snipers around the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to the VRS? That your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes. The whole area around Sarajevo, let's say, following the -- any unit that was at the confrontation lines. Or just behind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I don't know about the other units. But in my battalion there were 12 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if they were sharpshooters by training, but they were given sniping rifles. I don't know how much knowledge they had about the weapons ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether there are others apart from those 12 around Sarajevo. If you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that lack of factual knowledge would make it very difficult for you to assess which was best equipped and trained for sniping?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would agree, but we would have five casualties per day, and that shows that they had very well trained people and good rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many casualties were there on the other side per day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many of those five were soldiers; how many of those five were civilians, a day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't always five per day, but when there were days like that, there would be two civilians, three soldiers, or people from civilian protection or that is to say, people from work platoons so ... it varied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed, and try to keep the witness to the facts rather than to judgement or opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, just a second, please, if I may consult with Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You always may consult with Mr. Mladic, as long as it is done at an inaudible volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Draskovic, since I was told that in line 25 on page 53 and line 1, page 54, of LiveNote there was some dilemmas, I would like to clarify certain matters with you. In your company, was there, in terms of establishment, any part of the sniper unit?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Never in that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the platoon within which there were sharpshooters, can you tell the Trial Chamber - if you know - who that platoon belonged to, where the snipers were as well?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: I may have misspoken. It was a squad of sharpshooters, 12 people. They were within the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to clarify. Let me just ask you something else. Do you know whether, in terms of establishment, in companies to your left and right, were there any snipers that belonged to these companies?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to take a look --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the map is not good enough then I'm going to use another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But first actually let me ask you this: You mentioned today, in direct and cross-examination, the Pavkovic motel. Does that building exist today in Sarajevo at all?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: It does not. I passed through that area about ten days ago, and it's been completely torn down. There's a building that was being built there but nothing happened. Since it had concrete walls and it was seriously fortified it was used a lot for sniper nests.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to show you a map of a Sarajevo and my request to you is to mark this building if you can, where the Pavkovic motel was. Because we discussed that during preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, P3, page 8. Could we please have that document in e-court, P3, page 8. We'll try using that first and maybe it's even going to be better in another document, P123, but we'll see where we manage to get better organised. So P3, page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Loading pictures usually takes a bit more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in, the central part of this photograph, F4.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can I just make a suggestion if we go to page 11, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have F -- the F4 incident on another page more specifically. If that would help, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure, Your Honour. Because of the distance of the place where the Pavkovic motel was. So I'm going to ask the witness first whether he can find his way in this photograph. If not, then could we use P123. Because there we also have the names of streets. So perhaps it would be better for the witness. But if the witness can deal with this because we did work during proofing with this map, then maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Witness, can you find your way here now?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot. Because there are no street names here. It's unclear to me. The Pavkovic motel was near our positions so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I really cannot manage with this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the stadium which is approximately, as far as we understand, in the centre of this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I see the stadium.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that assist you also looking at where the river Miljacka is? Does this assist you in finding the location where the Pavkovic, Milan Pavkovic motel has been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the left of the Zeljeznicar football club stadium, but there are no street names here and my eyesight is not good so that is perhaps why I cannot actually see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, without your leave without having it broadcast can we have P123. Let's try that way. P123.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And -- yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I would actually, given -- if we could go into private session for a moment, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Can you find your bearings on this map, Witness? You see in the centre Grbavica. And do you see the Miljacka river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map is much better, clearer. I'm just trying to locate the motel now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could assist. Yes, let get back to the visible image again. Now this is not exactly the same as what we saw before. Now we are back. And we zoomed into the centre of this earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do try, you see the Vrace memorial park now. And you had that cross there --

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: I see Moravska, Jadranska --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The Grbavica stadium?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly it's in this area. Somewhere around this location. That's where the motel was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now mark that with a little circle?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly here. Somewhere around here, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- has the witness a marker? Because I don't see any marking at this moment -- oh, yes, I now see where the marking is. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, and I can see it on the screen in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I now do as well. Witness, could you please put a -- clear letters PM for Pavkovic motel next to where you marked this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, roughly here, the little circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But ... well, that's -- the P is to the left of the marked circle; the M is to the right of it. So it looks, more or less, like POM or ROM and that's where the witness marked the Pavkovic motel. You want to tender this, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no other markings needed?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28112a, with the marks receives exhibit number D1201, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check. I think it had a small a to it as well. So it should be 28112a which has now received number D1201, as marked by the witness. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With -- with the greatest respect, Your Honour, and the transcript has it correctly, 28112a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I added the 8 and the A were apparently confused. Apologies for not getting this right immediately. So I now repeat 28112a has been assigned D1201 and is admitted into evidence. Further questions, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. We would like to thank you and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, anything further?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just for about five minutes, Your Honours, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Draskovic, you keep reaffirming - you've done it twice today to my friend - that you never once received an order for any offensive operations. But, again, just so that we can set the record straight, it's a fact, isn't it, that your units took control of the area of Grbavica 1 and the Vrbanja bridge on the 4th of May, 1992 in offensive operations; right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly, that was the beginning of the war. But I was not in the area then. I took my family away, so I was not there at the time, and I cannot speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, were you in the area on the 5th of June, 1992 when your units took control of Soping and Grbavica 2 in offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my unit did not take part in these operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And were you in the area on 17 June 1992 when, let's say, your brigade occupied Zlatiste, took control of Zlatiste in offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DRASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the area of my company.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Draskovic, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, either by the parties or by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness or would we first -- no. Are you ready, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can make a break if it suits you better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't suit us specifically better, because I think we're still 20 minutes off from the usual break time but if you would prefer to take the break now and then to start the examination of the next witness for the next 65 minutes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can continue now, then, Your Honour. We would call Ms. Biljana Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And she's waiting for a while, I take it, so, therefore, could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Stojkovic, I assume. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Ms. Stojkovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic -- and you find him to your left. In a second, he will be standing. Mr. Mladic is supposed not to greet witnesses. Mr. Mladic, is that clear? You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask the usher to give Ms. Stojkovic's, her written statement. Can you show it to the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Ms. Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please slowly state your name and surname for the record.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Biljana Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we speak the same language, I'm going to pause after your answers. That does not mean that I'm not satisfied with the answer. At one point in time, did you give a statement to the members of General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens 1D1750, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Stojkovic, on the right-hand side of the screen before you, can you see a document?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see a signature on the first page of that document?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's my own signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this page, Ms. Stojkovic, can you see a signature?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review your statement before testifying today?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was recorded in this statement, has it been recorded correctly; that is to say, is it exactly what you said to the members of General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is contained in the statement, to the best of your knowledge, is it correct and true?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct and true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, Ms. Stojkovic, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would offer this statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Melikian, no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01750 receives exhibit number D1202, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will read short statement summary for Ms. Stojkovic. Ms. Stojkovic, Biljana, is a journalist living in Belgrade Serbia. She earned her Ph.D. degree in the field of development strategy at the military academy of the university of defence. Witness will testify that on the 16th of July, 1995, she married Mr. Zarko Stojkovic in Voznjesenska Church in Belgrade Serbia. She will confirm that on wedding ceremony, their godfathers were Ratko and Bosiljka Mladic as well as they were present in Belgrade on this date. On the same wedding day, they were in restaurant Dva Ribara in Belgrade. Ms. Stojkovic will testify about the whereabouts of General Mladic on the 16th of July, 1995. That was the short statement. I will have only a few questions for Ms. Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put them to the witness, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Stojkovic, we have your statement which is now in evidence. I will just seek a few clarifications with you.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You explained when General Mladic arrived at your place with his wife. You explained the time spent at the restaurant and in the church. Throughout that time, could you observe that General Mladic had some communications means with him and that he was using them, being military staff you know what they look like?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was surprised myself. He seemed to be fully focussed on our wedding and the celebrations attached to it in Serbia, which means he was fully dedicated to the people present, the procedure entailed by the church ceremony, the time spent with the bride and groom at the restaurant. He seemed to be fully focussed on the time he spent with us and our family. He had no communication devices on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, do you remember when General Mladic and his wife left your wedding?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think I pointed it out in my statement. It was around 5.30. I don't know whether it was a minute or two before or later, but definitely around 5.30 or quarter to 6.00, that is when he left the dining hall at the Dva Ribara restaurant where the ceremonial lunch took place. He excused himself, citing official duties. I stayed in the dining hall with my guests, while my husband escorted him to the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Stojkovic, thank you. This is all that General Mladic's Defence had for you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Ms. Melikian, are you ready could cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I took it you wanted to rely upon our ability to draw conclusions, that if the 17th of July is the day after that it must have been the 16th, although it's found nowhere, I think, in the statement that it all happened on the 16th. And where the witness said that she already said in her statement that it was 5.30, I tried to find that, but I was unable to immediately find that. But you left us some small puzzles but we're able to resolve them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah in paragraph 17 -- 11, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's where we could conclude that it was all about the 16th and there seems to be no dispute about that. Ms. Melikian, I take it, that the wedding took place on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: No, there's no dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, basically, you start with times and places if you take a statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have failed to introduce you. Ms. Melikian will now cross-examine you. Ms. Melikian is counsel for the Prosecution, and you find her to your right, as you've seen her already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Ms. Stojkovic, you say in your statement at paragraphs 6 and 7 that you begin the morning at your apartment and then you proceed to the church. At about what time did you arrive at the church?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I see there are some problems with certain terms, because I was rather general in my statement and I can try and clarify the situation by hour by hour. I spend the night in my apartment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just answer the questions, then Ms. Melikian will exactly ask you what she'd like to know. And the first thing is: At what time did you arrive at the church.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We left the apartment at 11.30. At 12.00, we had the wedding ceremony. At 2.00 p.m., we had lunch at the Dva Ribara restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: So I arrived at the restaurant at around 2.00?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: And was there a meal served at the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It takes a long time back in Serbia just a serving of the meals takes about two hours. So we were there between 2.00 p.m. and 6.00 p.m., at the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: And I think you may have mentioned this earlier in your direct examination, but was Mr. Mladic, was he with you the whole time in the restaurant or ...

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, we were there all the time. That is what I was trying to explain. The first person to enter my apartment was the hairdresser, at around 8.00. She was followed quarter of an hour later by the cameraman and then my husband's family arrived, followed by the best man and that matron of honour. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... the question was only about the time you spent at the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were asked only about the time in the restaurant. Could you answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean the time I spent with the guests there or the time spent at the restaurant by the best man and the matron of honour with us and the other guests?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was about Mr. Mr. Mladic spent all the time when you were in the restaurant with you, with the company which was in the restaurant. Was that the question, Ms. Melikian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He spent all that time with us and never left the restaurant, either he or his wife, between 2.00 p.m. and 5.30. He was in the restaurant throughout that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: But he got up from the table during that time and maybe left the dining-room? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I would have to acquaint you with the layout of the restaurant. It was on the middle floor, below us was ground floor and behind the restaurant is the toilet linked to the restaurant so he did not even leave the middle floor, let alone the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: So he didn't get up from the table from when you arrived at the restaurant at around 2.00 p.m. until when he left at 5.30, he didn't leave the dining-room where you were?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: You understood me well. He only got up when he was supposed to give the toast. I don't know whether you are familiar with the significance of toasting in our culture.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: I don't know that I am. I guess I'm just -- to -- just to be clear, did he ever -- you said he stood up to give a toast. Did you ever stand up to go to the restroom?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. I really don't remember that he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one question. When you were asked about whether he ever got up from the table, your answer was about where the restrooms are, where the toilets are. That, in view of the question, comes a bit as a surprise because it wasn't asked. Do you consider it a possibility that he went to the restrooms although you are convinced that he didn't leave the floor on which the restaurant was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm wondering about the sense of this. His wife was seated next to me and he was next to her. So he was my second person to the left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please answer my question. My question is: And I pointed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to say this. If he wanted to go to the toilet he must have passed next to me so I would have seen him. The only hypothetical possibility that I did not see him was that we dance at our weddings and at some point perhaps we danced, we waltzed or something of the sort. If something goes on four hours I cannot exclude that hypothetical possibility but as far as what I could see, he did not go to the toilet. Does that clarify the situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, half it does. Because you explain why you may have missed it and at the same time you say you didn't see him go. That's not fully consistent. But let's leave it for that for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Moving on briefly to another topic, you mention that there were wedding tapes of -- that your wedding was filmed and that these tapes were subsequently stolen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Fully correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: I'm just curious. You said in paragraph 11 that you -- of your statement that you watched the videotapes the next day.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Do you remember if these videotapes had a date and time stamp on them?

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: They did have a date and --

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you please repeat your answer. I don't think it was interpreted.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If we had the possibility to present the tape to the Court designated as wedding 1 and wedding 2, it would have been the strongest point to prove at what point in time, at what hour and minute General Mladic was at the wedding table and how he spent his time at my wedding. It means that there was a time code on the tape in terms of what took place when.

utterances.speaker: MS. MELIKIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: BILJANA STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have a question for a clarification. Again, about timing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. You said, this can be found on page 69, line 6 and 7. You said, "so we were there," that means in the restaurant, "between 2.00 p.m. and 6.00." Later, page 70, lines 6 and 7, you said: He spent all the time with us and never left the restaurant either he or his wife between 2.00 and 5.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Therefore I would like to ask you: Was he there until 6.00 or 5.30? We have received two time-frames from you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for that question. The situation is as follows. All guests arrived at 2.00 p.m. and we entered the dining hall, including General Mladic and his wife. They were the first guests to leave, leaving at 5.30. Unless I also included my colleague, the cameraman who, having spent the first tape left at 5.00 to buy a new one. But the guests left at different times following that. My husband and I remained as the last ones. For example, some guests for their private obligations left around 6.00. Some left around 8.00. Let's say we left at around -- well, between 8.00 and 9.00 p.m. The band left at around 8.00 because they play at a different restaurant at Skadarlija. Then my husband, my father-in-law, and a few others took up instruments and sang and played for the guests. We stayed for another hour because we had rented the hall until, say, 8.00 or 9.00. Then we went to our apartment where some of the younger guests remained until early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that explain it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have received what you wanted to say. That means --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- after 5.30 that day, you haven't seen Mr. Mladic anymore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are fully correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. You were asked whether Mr. Mladic had no communications devices on him and -- you said you had no communication devices on him. May I take it that you meant to say that you didn't see any communication devices? Because he may have had them somewhere you couldn't see. So it's -- do I have to understand that you didn't see any of those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We certainly did not search our guests at the wedding. I hope you understand. What I did not see was that he displayed any such device or used it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how I thought I would have to understand it but I just wanted to be sure that that's what you meant. I have no further questions. Mr. Lukic, any questions triggered by the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only question of video and then I would just continue with pictures whether they were missing, whether some of them were retrieved because I think we have some pictures in our evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have examined the witness in-chief, didn't you? And would you now revisit matters which are ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought if you are interested I could, but I don't see it as necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a question whether you would have -- want to put that before us and if that's the case, of course, the appropriate way of doing it would have been to do it during examination-in-chief -- Mr. Mladic, no comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkovic is coming after his wife and I can deal with it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't arise from cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no other questions either? The Judges also have no further questions for you. Therefore, Ms. Stojkovic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered not that many but at least the questions that you were put to you both by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your kindness and professionalism.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was time for the break already a bit earlier, but we'll take the break now and we'll resume at a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are calling Mr. Stojkovic, Zarko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stojkovic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated, Mr. Stojkovic. Mr. Stojkovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will pause after your answers so as to give the interpreters time to interpret. For the record, kindly state your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Zarko Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkovic, did you at some point in time provide a statement to the members of General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D1751 on our screens. [In English] Can I kindly ask the usher to provide Mr. Stojkovic with his written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojkovic, you have your statement in hard copy, and you can see it on your right-hand side screen. On the first page, do you see a signature?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: My own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see a signature on this page as well?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Also mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkovic, did you have occasion to review your statement before today's testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does -- do the contents of the statement, as put on paper, correctly and fairly state what you mentioned to the members of General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is what is contained in the statement truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions today, would you provide basically the same answers?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In full.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender Mr. Stojkovic's statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01751 receives Exhibit D1203, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1203 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would have some questions after we read short summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please read it and then put the questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Zarko Stojkovic was an officer in VJ. He will testify that he married Biljana Stojkovic born Djurdjevic on 16 July 1995 in Voznjesenjska church in Belgrade. He will confirm that their godfathers were Ratko and Bosiljka Mladic, as well as that they were present in Belgrade on this date. On the same wedding day, they were in a restaurant, Dva Ribara, in Belgrade. And that was short statement summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put the questions to the witness you had on your mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojkovic, today we were able to hear that the video recording of your wedding disappeared from your mother-in-law's home. What was the fate of the photographs from the wedding?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The fate of the photographs was similar to the fate of the tapes, meaning the part of the photographs that were to go to mother-in-law also disappeared while we were out of the country on official business. They disappeared from the house in Krusevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were some photographs preserved and, if so, where? Who had them? Were you able to get to some of them later on?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When we returned to the country, some of the photographs were still in some of the children's photo albums, but now they are gone too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These were the photographs of your children or --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: These were the photographs of our best man and matron of honour with our children and with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you able to locate any wedding photographs after all?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: There are a few, and they are also in my mother-in-law's home. As for the photographs that we had, we were never able to find them. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask a question. How did the photographs in your possession disappear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't precisely answer that question, given the fact that I was away and out of the country at the time it took place. Several times during our absence, my mother-in-law's house was burglarised and there are also official records of that made by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that the photos that were in your mother-in-law's house disappeared and there were burglaries but you talked about photographs in your possession and I'm asking about those ones that were in your possession, how did they disappear not the ones at your mother's place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps there was a misunderstanding. I apologise and I will clarify some things. All the photographs, albums, and tapes that had to do with the wedding were left in my mother-in-law's house during our absence from the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what -- the photographs that you -- were in your children's albums, where were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The albums were also handed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of your statement, you say that the wedding took place on the 16th of July, 1995. We asked about your best man and matron of honour. I wanted to briefly ask you whether you remember between what times were General Mladic and his wife Bosiljka in your company on 16th July, 1995 and at which locations?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Ratko and Bosiljka Mladic arrived on the 16th of July around 10.00 at our apartment in Narodni Front Street in Belgrade. They were with us until we left to the -- for the church which took place between 12.00 and 2.00. After that, at the Dva Ribara restaurant, we continued with a lunch and celebrations until 5.30 or 5.45 when I personally saw them off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the apartment where you were in the street Narodni Front, well, you're a military man, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see the general in that apartment around 10.00? You say that he and his wife arrived? Did he use any communications equipment or a telephone?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not. Neither one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to ask although it may seem illogical, in church, or in front of the church, so related to the church wedding itself, did the general have any communications equipment and did he use any such thing?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I noticed - and do allow me to say - that during the wedding party itself that ensued, no communication equipment was used, not a telephone either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that you saw off your best man and that matron of honour after the wedding party. How far did you see them off?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did General Mladic drive that car or was it somebody else?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you wait for General Mladic and his wife to get into the car?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see the interior of the car?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that car, did you notice any communications equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkovic, this was brief. Your statement has already been admitted into evidence. Thank you. This is all that the Defence of General Mladic had for you at this moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I give an opportunity to cross-examine the witness, Judge Fluegge would have one or more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojkovic. You told us about the photo albums given to your mother-in-law. How many were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One for each child.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't know the number of your children.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Two. Two albums. Two children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who put -- who compiled these photo albums? Who put these photos in the albums?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally and my wife Biljana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: From whom did you receive those photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are photographs from family celebrations. So these are our personal photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Made by your own photo equipment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You, yourself, and your family members took these photos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. Family members and we.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I ask you these questions because I don't see any reference is to photo albums and photos in your statement. In your statement, paragraph 8 and 9, you are talking about cassettes received from cameraman, Radovan Popovic. Can you explain that further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the question was related only to the wedding, it was cassettes that were related to the wedding. However, this is personal, and it was not a subject that was a subject of the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You, in answering questions by the -- by Mr. Lukic, you referred to photo albums. And in your statement we have received now in evidence, you are talking about cassettes from cameraman Radovan Popovic. I don't fully understand why, in the statement, you are referring to cassettes and in your examination-in-chief you are referring to photo albums with photographs, you explained, taken by you and family members.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in relation to this, I shall repeat what I said and shall expand the statement that I made since we were talking about cassettes all the time, because these cassettes were recorded on the day of the 16th of July; whereas, the albums pertain to a certain period of time of our family life and pictures that do not pertain to that period. That is why there weren't any questions about cassettes and pictures, since, now, the question was about pictures with General Mladic, and we were talking about cassettes because they were related to the day of the 16th of July, when our wedding took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I understand it better now. And what was stolen by the burglaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean what was stolen where? My mother-in-law's house? Are we talking about the Krusevac case? Is that what you mean? I do apologise. But if you could kindly explain this to me a bit. Which location do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The residence of your mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hm. After we took a look and when this happened, we realised that the cassettes and pictures were missing from family celebrations and from the wedding, those that were at the house of my mother-in-law in Krusevac. Now whether they were stolen, I personally did not state any such thing, nor would I dare do that because I am not a competent organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for answering these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey. Mr. McCloskey is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, although for not more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We know you're a military man. Are you retired or are in active service or reserves?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Active service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what's your current rank?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Colonel, well, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In Uzicka Pozega in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I grew up in Pozega until I finished elementary school and then I left in order to continue my schooling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you were -- were you in the VJ, the -- from 1992 through 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you participate in any of the wars that occurred, beginning 1991, in Croatia or Bosnia or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not participate in the war in Bosnia in that period. In the period of 1991 and 1992, I was carrying out duties within the Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA, securing the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you get to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you ever present in any war theatre from 1991 through the end of the war in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It depends on what is meant by "war theatre" in that period. Could you please be more specific when putting that question to me? Does it pertain to the region or what was it that you meant?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you in Bosnia during the Bosnian war.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You never went to Bosnia during the war period?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We didn't get your short response --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It was just "for" and did not continue the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So you never even travelled to Bosnia between May 1992 and December 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you assist the war effort for the VRS in any way?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I find that question to be unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was your specialty in, let's say, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO STOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, I was in school in Belgrade, when I got married. I arrived Belgrade in 1994 for my schooling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what was your specialty in 1993 were you armour, infantry or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I see it's quarter past 2.00. Therefore, we'll adjourn for the day. Mr. Stojkovic, we'll have to adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 but I hereby instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, and that includes your wife, or communicate in any other way about your testimony. Now, I think it would be -- you're not allowed to talk about your testimony. Talking about the testimony of your wife would come down to the same because it touches upon the same subject matter, so you should refrain from any conversation with whomever, including your wife, about the events on the 16th of July, 1995 or anything related to that. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 20th of August, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of August, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
